title: All Should Be Equal in the Eyes of Language Models: Counterfactually Aware Fair Text Generation
benchmark_measurement: The benchmarks measured stereotypical associations and sentiment bias in contexts involving religion. Specifically, StereoSet and CrowS-Pairs measured the models' preference for stereotypical sentences over anti-stereotypical ones, while the BOLD dataset was used to measure the mean and standard deviation of sentiment in text generated about different religious ideologies.
findings: The proposed method, CAFIE, significantly reduced stereotypical bias related to religion across all tested models (GPT-2 Small, GPT-2 Large, Pythia). On the CrowS-Pairs benchmark, CAFIE showed a 15.3% improvement for the religion attribute, bringing the bias score closer to the ideal unbiased value. On the StereoSet benchmark, it also consistently lowered the stereotype score for religion, indicating a reduction in harmful associations.
